title: Is it safe?
speaker: coach
source: DRAFT: check against official guidelines (for example ERC or AHA Basic Life Support)
line: A man has just collapsed on the sidewalk in front of you. What do you do first?

choices.text: Look around: is it safe for me to go to him? (traffic, electricity, fire...)
choices.feedback: Right: you can't help him if you get hurt too.

choices.text: Run straight to him without looking
choices.feedback: Stop! Check for danger first, or there could be two victims.

choices.text: Film the scene for the paramedics
choices.feedback: No time for that. Check for danger, then act.

title: Does he respond?
speaker: coach
source: DRAFT: check against official guidelines (for example ERC or AHA Basic Life Support)
line: It's safe. You kneel next to him. How do you check if he is conscious?

choices.text: Gently shake his shoulders and ask loudly: "Are you OK?"
Wait a minute to see if he wakes up

choices.feedback: Too rough. Shake his shoulders gently and talk loudly.

title: Is he breathing?
speaker: coach
source: DRAFT: check against official guidelines (for example ERC or AHA Basic Life Support)
line: He doesn't respond. You tilt his head back and look, listen and feel for breathing, for no more than 10 seconds. He only makes a few slow gasps. Is that normal breathing?

choices.text: No: slow gasps are not normal breathing. His heart has probably stopped.
choices.feedback: Exactly. Gasps are a sign of cardiac arrest.

choices.text: Yes, he is breathing, so I just wait
choices.feedback: Slow gasps are NOT normal breathing. Treat it as a cardiac arrest.

title: Call for help
speaker: coach
source: DRAFT: check against official guidelines, and the emergency number of your country
line: He doesn't respond and isn't breathing normally. What do you do now?

choices.text: Call 112 and put the phone on speaker
choices.feedback: Speaker mode keeps your hands free for compressions.

choices.text: Drive him to the hospital myself
choices.feedback: Too slow, and dangerous. Call 112: help comes to you.

choices.text: Call a friend to ask what to do
choices.feedback: Call 112: the dispatcher is trained to guide you.

choices.text: A man collapsed. He doesn't respond and isn't breathing normally. We're at [address].
choices.feedback: Clear and complete: what happened, his state, and where you are.
The dispatcher needs details: what happened, his state, and your address.

title: The defibrillator
speaker: dispatcher
line: Is there a defibrillator nearby? You see someone else coming to help.

choices.text: Ask that person to bring the defibrillator while I start compressions
Leave him alone and look for the defibrillator myself
choices.feedback: Don't leave him: send someone else, and start compressions.
